speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The tunnel was built in 2007 by the state and continues to be owned and operated by the state, working with utility suppliers and developments in the area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It contains the electricity cables, telecommunications cables, water pipes and district cooling pipes for the air-conditioning of buildings in the area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We decided to build the CST because it offers many advantages over the conventional way utility networks are laid.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Traditionally, different utility lines are laid separately under the roads.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means that the road has to be opened whenever there is a need to lay a new utility line, or to maintain and repair existing lines, for example, when there is a burst pipe.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This can lead to repeated traffic disruptions and diversions, as well as nuisance to pedestrians and other users.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Furthermore, because the utility lines are spread out in an ad hoc manner as and when they are laid, there is a risk that subsequent construction or road works may lead to accidental damage to pipes and cables and potentially disrupt utility supplies in the area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The CST is intended to mitigate these risks and issues.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Once the tunnel is built, utility lines can be installed and maintained in the tunnel without opening up the road again, thereby, eliminating lane closures and disruptive works.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When there is a fault in any of the utility lines, repairs can be carried out simply by entering the tunnel.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The tunnel also enhances the reliability of services as it provides robust protection for the utilities housed within it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By consolidating all utilities within the CST, we also optimise the use of underground space, leaving room for other infrastructure like pedestrian underpasses.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The CST, therefore, improves the efficiency and reliability of utility services while raising the quality of our urban living environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This way of planning and building infrastructure calls for new operational and administrative practices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So far, we have relied on contractual and administrative arrangements to facilitate the maintenance and operation of the CST in Marina Bay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Bill will apply to any gazetted "CST area".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For now, the only gazetted CST area will be Marina Bay and the intention is to gazette the area containing all developments which receive their utility supplies from the CST.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If and when they build new CSTs in the future, we will also apply the provisions of the Bill to them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is already the case at Marina Bay, where utility suppliers are not allowed to lay their lines directly into the ground.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, to facilitate the efficient functioning of the CST, the Bill gives authorised persons power to enter any land or premises in the CST area for the purposes of operating and maintaining the CST.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Access to the CST is provided through ancillary structures located on private land, such as entrances, passageways connecting entrances, and ventilation shafts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These entrances and ventilation shafts are integrated with buildings adjacent to the CST.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was how we planned for the CST at Marina Bay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We did so consciously so that we would not have unsightly standalone structures spoiling the streetscape or taking up space.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To operate and maintain the CST, various persons will need access to these ancillary structures to get into the CST.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will include technicians from utility companies to lay or maintain their lines, public officers to carry out inspections and contractors to operate the facilities in the tunnel and to perform routine functions like cleaning or security checks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, access is secured administratively through agreements with individual building owners and occupiers, but these agreements will not automatically be passed on to subsequent owners and occupiers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this provision in the Bill ensures access to the CST through ancillary structures for operations and maintenance, regardless of building ownership and occupiers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, to ensure that access to and functioning of the CST are not impeded, the Bill also empowers officers to require persons to remove obstructions to entrances and ventilation shafts and to return these structures to their original condition.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the specified person fails to comply, the officer can rectify the situation and recover the costs from that person.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, the Bill requires building owners or their tenants to take reasonable measures to maintain the ancillary structures on their land.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Officers may require such persons to carry out works reasonably deemed necessary to keep these structures in working order.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If they fail to comply, officers or their contractors may carry out the required works and recover the costs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This provision is necessary because the integrated ancillary structures are physically part of the private building, built by the owner, and wear and tear generally results from the usage and occupancy of the building.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is the responsibility of the building owner to maintain the building, including the ancillary structures within it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In key areas like Marina Bay, this could have severe economic consequences.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the works are carried out without approval, officers may order the works to be stopped or require rectification works to be carried out.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have described the key provisions in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is an underground infrastructure which will enable us to improve the way we lay and maintain utility networks and utility lines in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will help us to optimise the use of space, it will enable us to build a better city and, ultimately, improve the quality of life for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Urban planning engineers often refer to the maze of pipes and conduits and shallow urban underground spaces as the spaghetti subsurface problem: a criss-crossing, multi-layered mess of water pipes, sewers, gas conduits, power lines, telephone and television cables that sit below many of our road surfaces today.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many would also have encountered the constant sight of digging, resurfacing and re-digging of the subsurface by multiple agencies and companies in the past.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, the CST, or multi-utilities tunnel, as they are called overseas, offers a sustainable solution that permits simple and safe operations on the infrastructures, avoiding recurring street works that are necessary for direct burial trenches.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As such, I would like to ask the Minister what the key challenges for the construction of the MBCST have been, as the construction face difficulties, thus, leading to the prolonged construction period.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Has maintenance of the tunnels been difficult for a largely reclaimed bay area?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If the area is also fast developing, has right of access been an issue so far that the Ministry has had to deal with?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What has been the feedback from current building owners that have to provide access to ancillary facilities of the CST through their buildings?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Has there been an increase in the initial investment costs for laying of cables and pipes compared to the usual trench burial method?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is right that with such a large capital investment and the large number of utilities that a CST supports, that the Government regulates and sets down as law the guidelines for access and adoption of use by building owners and utility-providers.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, CSTs are not new in the international sphere and have been planned for in Singapore since the late 1990s.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Is there a reason for the long time lapse before the introduction of this Bill before the House?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Is it in response to violations or potential violations?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last year, the Minister also announced that by 2019, the URA will be releasing the pilot projects under the underground masterplan.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Does the Ministry see the CST as a future model for new developments, both commercial and residential, as well as redevelopment sites?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Jurong Lake District has been identified as one such area for the introduction of the CST, together with the Punggol Digital Corridor.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will the Ministry also consider residential towns, such as Bidadari, Tengah and the freed-up Paya Lebar airbase, as new areas for the introduction of CST, in place of the traditional trench burial techniques?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will the Ministry ensure that there can be economies of scale, considering the very high upfront infrastructure costs that accompany CST projects?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Alex Yam asked if the Government has faced challenges constructing, maintaining and operating the Marina Bay CST.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It took time for us to plan ahead and to make the investments in the project.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So far, where maintenance and operations are concerned, we have enjoyed the cooperation of utility suppliers, developers and building owners.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if we have to do a new project, if we have to work with new parties, or if we are going to build a new CST elsewhere, we would want the legal and regulatory framework to be very clear, so that we can continue to provide utility services of the highest standards, without any hiccups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Hence, we are now putting these provisions into the Bill.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When formulating the Bill, we had consulted the building owners at Marina Bay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They provided useful feedback, for instance, on the way the CST could be better designed and constructed and, where possible, we will take this feedback into account for future developments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Alex Yam asked whether the Government sees the CSTs as a model to serve new development areas in the future, be it for commercial or residential areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Indeed, there is potential for CSTs in new developments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as significant capital investment is required for the CST, it would make more economic sense to do this in an area of sufficient size with major new developments that need to be serviced by multiple utilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We can then bring together all the utility lines underground and then better optimise the use of space.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have mentioned earlier, this Bill clarifies and enhances the Government's regulatory practices to ensure the safe and efficient operation of CSTs in Singapore.      .
